findings.title: ADR 0023's withheld writer/anchor table is false for two of eight reasons, and "the partition is exactly RenderWithholdReason" is false — following it stamps occurred_at, the single retention clock, with a render timestamp

Fragile assertion: expect(entry?.reason).toMatch(/cascade/i) passes on the exact negation of the claim it guards — the identical defect class this PR already fixed once, in a sibling file, in the same change

C5's outer IS TRUE wrapper is asserted by nothing: no row can reach it (proved) and no assertion reads C5's definition — while C1's identical wrapper and migration 114's precedent are both pinned structurally
Three plan-artifact citations that were true at the merge base are stale at HEAD, staled by this change's own edits — including deviation D8, which exists to correct that exact citation
The terminal purge failure this diff newly makes reachable emits account_offboarding_purge_failed, which no runbook rule row routes — all six facets MISSING, and neither generic sink covers it
"nine probe rows, all nine now correct" — the table immediately below lists eight; repeated verbatim in the arch-review-log entry
CONTEXT.md asserts in the present tense two tabs on /dashboard/analytics — Metrics and Restraint — neither of which exists; the page renders AnalyticsContent with no tab UI
Retry and terminal captures share one constant message and no fingerprint, so any first-seen rule added for RT-05 fires once, on a warning retry, and never on the terminal error

The in-test comment misattributes the ['different', NULL] rejection to array_position "plus the outer IS TRUE wrapper"; with array_position present that row's first arm is FALSE, not NULL, so the wrapper contributes nothing to it
ADR 0023 maps admin_halt "on outreach_withheld", a lane whose rows cannot carry it — migration 111 permits admin_halt only under delivery_status cancelled

C5's all_refusal_codes IS NOT NULL and cardinality(...) > 0 are provably redundant — zero differing rows over the whole value space — so no row pins them, and the two suite cases whose titles suggest they do actually reject via other clauses
findings.rejected_reason: Deliberate defence in depth, not dead weight. `all_refusal_codes IS NOT NULL` and `cardinality(...) > 0` are redundant only GIVEN the sibling clauses that currently stand; each states one fact the reader of supabase/migrations/116_refusal_events.sql:157-166 needs, and removing them would make a later edit to array_position or to C4 silently widen the constraint. The same reasoning is applied to C5's outer IS TRUE, which RT-03 correctly showed is also unreachable by any row and which is now pinned STRUCTURALLY rather than deleted.

findings.title: Three minor doc inaccuracies: the 108'S typo; an arch-review-log rule attributed to deployment-guide II.5 which that section does not state; and the intake attributing "eleven Refusal write sites" to #1010-#1013 while the migration header and log put the first caller in #1009

authorizations.approval_text: Accept the risk, file a follow-up. Rationale: the gap predates this branch, the failure path is only reachable in a window the ship order already closes (production DDL lands before the code), and a runbook rule is a distinct piece of ops work that deserves its own review rather than being appended to a schema PR. Follow-up filed as RepWorth/ai-review-responder#1016.
